ERR-005 • Ewell (Williamsburg), Virginia & Llanfair PG, Anglesey, Wales • 1996–Present (Originally recorded as The Winter Palace)

The Arctic Symphony Project

Holiday Symphonic Rock, Neoclassical Metal & Trilingual Winter Operas

Born on a freezing December night in 1996 when the Rowlands and Harrison siblings turned their Williamsburg living room into an emergency broadcast studio to guide abducted 14-year-old Julian ("Julep") home across the Appalachian Mountains with "Upon This Winter's Night."

What Kind of Music Is The Arctic Symphony Project? Sweeping Trans-Siberian-scale symphonic rock, soaring distorted electric guitars, Baroque cello counter-melodies, silver glockenspiel, Brahms music-box motifs, and trilingual choirs (Cymraeg Welsh, Québécois French, and English).

Canonical In-Universe History

1. Canonical Band Lore & Sanctuary History

December 1996: The Appalachian Radio Beacon ("Upon This Winter's Night")

When fourteen-year-old Julian Rowlands was abducted toward Ohio in December 1996 without his custom wheelchair, his older twin siblings Gabriel and Gwendolyn and twins Maria and Clara transformed their Ewell, Virginia living room into a war room. Sampling Julian's cherished brass Brahms "Wiegenlied" music box and pairing it with roaring electric guitars, cello, and silver glockenspiel, they pressed the track to DAT and convinced late-night FM engineers along the Blue Ridge and Appalachian mountain spine to broadcast "Upon This Winter's Night" every hour on the hour—giving Julian a coded acoustic compass that he had not been forgotten.

The Vanguard Horizon Vault & The 2007 Trilingual Liberation

In 1996, predatory label Vanguard Horizon forced the family to cut a 3-minute English-only radio edit while locking their full 5-minute Welsh (Cymraeg), Québécois French, and Trilingual "Family Mix" masters in a corporate vault. A decade later, in 2007, Samantha and Engine Room Records acquired and liquidated Vanguard Horizon's catalog—returning 100% of the master tapes to the Rowlands family.

Tales from the Solstice (3-Disc Symphonic Rock Opera)

With their masters liberated, the ensemble re-christened themselves The Arctic Symphony Project and recorded the 3-disc symphonic rock opera Tales from the Solstice (2007), uniting Julian's 1996 Appalachian beacon with Matthew's cross-country survival and culminating in the restored Trilingual "Family Mix" of "Upon This Winter's Night." Read the complete companion novel Upon This Winter's Night: The Story of Julian Rowlands at books.raggiesoft.com/books/julian.

2007 Studio Album 31 Tracks

Tales from the Solstice

The 2007 3-Disc Symphonic Holiday Rock Opera

A sweeping 3-disc symphonic rock opera uniting two survivors across a decade. Originally forged on December 11, 1996 in Ewell, Virginia, 'Upon This Winter's Night' was recorded in a spare bedroom and broadcast across the Appalachian radio towers by Gabriel and Gwendolyn Rowlands and twins Maria and Clara Harrison to guide their fourteen-year-old brother Julian ('Julep') home from his abduction to Ohio. Ten years later, after learning that their 1997 single served as the 'Sonic Armor' that grounded nineteen-year-old Matthew during his cross-country abduction from Norfolk to Seattle and rescue by Jyn, Samantha bought out Vanguard Horizon's vaults—commissioning the family to compose the 3-disc rock opera telling Matthew's cross-country ordeal and liberating Julian's vaulted Trilingual 'Family Mix' (Cymraeg, Québécois French, and US English).

Artist Profile
  • Genre: Symphonic Rock / Neoclassical Rock Opera
  • Active: 1996–Present
  • Origin: Ewell (Williamsburg), VA & Llanfair PG, Anglesey, Wales
  • Core Ensemble: Gabriel Rowlands, Gwendolyn Rowlands, Maria Harrison-Rowlands, Clara Harrison, Marcus, Sarah & Julian “Julep” Rowlands
  • Key Sound: Heavy Cello, Distorted Guitars, Silver Glockenspiel, Trilingual Choir (Cymraeg / Québécois / English)
The Liberation of the Vault:
Originally formed in December 1996 as The Winter Palace when Gabriel and Gwendolyn Rowlands and twins Maria and Clara Harrison turned their Ewell living room into a war room to broadcast “Upon This Winter's Night” across the Appalachian radio towers and bring fourteen-year-old Julian home from his abduction to Ohio.
After Vanguard Horizon locked the family's Cymraeg, Québécois French, and Trilingual masters in a corporate vault in 1996, Samantha intervened a decade later—buying out Vanguard Horizon in 2007 to return the masters to the Rowlands family, liberate the Trilingual “Family Mix,” and commission the 3-disc rock opera Tales from the Solstice uniting Julian's beacon with Matthew's survival.

Featured Release

Tales from the Solstice (3-Disc Rock Opera)

A sweeping 3-disc symphonic holiday rock opera uniting Julian Rowlands' 1996 Appalachian rescue beacon with Matthew's cross-country abduction from Norfolk to Seattle and rescue by Jyn—culminating in the liberated 5-minute Trilingual “Family Mix” of “Upon This Winter's Night.”

Includes both the US English Studio Master & the Trilingual “Family Mix” (Cymraeg / Québécois / English)
